title: Greifvorrichtung zum Greifen von ferromagnetischen Gegenständen mit gekrümmter Oberfläche

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0030) The gripper device includes a gripper base body (housing) and contact elements (pole shoes) for gripping, and a magnetizing device with a magnet.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0035) The magnet is displaceable along a magnet displacement axis between an active configuration (gripping) and a passive configuration (release).

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0032) The contact elements (pole shoes) each have a contact section with a contact surface for engagement with the workpiece.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0036) The contact elements are arranged to guide the magnetic flux from the magnet to the contact surfaces to grip the object.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0039) The reference discloses that the contact elements can form a flat contact surface, and that the displacement axes are parallel to the gripping direction. This implies a 180° angle, but the range of 170-190° is not explicitly stated.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0030) The reference discloses a gripper with a housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes. It also implies the contact surface is parallel to the displacement direction, but the specific angle range of 170-190° is not explicitly mentioned.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0036) The reference describes the magnet in the active configuration creating a magnetic flux through the contact elements to grip the ferromagnetic object.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0033) The reference states that the displacement axes of the contact elements are parallel to each other and that the gripper is pressed along a gripping direction parallel to these axes. It does not explicitly state that the housing extends along a longitudinal axis parallel to this displacement direction, but this is implied by the overall design.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0032) The reference mentions contact sections and surfaces on the pole shoes that guide the magnetic field, but does not explicitly describe an 'active structure' beyond the general shape of the contact elements.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles on the contact surfaces of the pole shoes.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0008) The reference mentions that contact elements can have a projection, such as a nose, cone, or hook, but does not explicitly describe multiple projections forming the workpiece contact surface to direct the magnetic field.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe adjacent projections with specific recess depth or length relationships.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe a separate positioning device on the gripper for the workpiece.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0019) The reference explicitly states that in the active configuration, a subset of contact elements will act as a magnetic south pole and another subset as a magnetic north pole.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: Die Antriebseinrichtung kann beispielsweise pneumatisch, hydraulisch, elektrisch und/oder mechanisch betrieben sein.
features.note: The reference states that the drive device for displacing the magnet can be operated pneumatically, hydraulically, electrically, and/or mechanically.
features.refuted: The quote describes a drive device (Antriebseinrichtung) that can be operated pneumatically, hydraulically, electrically, or mechanically, but does not specify that this is a magnet or that it moves between gripping and release positions.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.quote: Beispielsweise kann die Sensoreinrichtung einen oder mehrere Anwesenheitssensoren umfassen, mittels denen erfassbar ist, ob sich ein Gegenstand an den Kontaktelementen befindet.
features.note: The reference discloses a sensor device that can include presence sensors to detect if an object is at the contact elements (workpiece sensor).
features.refuted: The quote describes presence sensors detecting whether an object is at contact elements, not specifically a position sensor for gripping/release positions or a sensor specifically for ferromagnetic workpieces.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0011) The reference mentions supply connections for external supply lines on the gripper base body (housing), but does not explicitly mention a receptacle for a workpiece sensor.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0011) The gripper base body (housing) can have a connecting device for attaching the gripping device to a manipulator, such as a robot flange.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.quote: Es ist grundsÃ¤tzlich auch denkbar, dass die Magnetisierungseinrichtung ein Abschirmelement umfasst, welches dazu ausgebildet ist, ein von dem Magnet bereitgestelltes magnetisches Feld abzuschirmen oder abzuschwÃ¤chen.
features.note: The reference mentions a shielding element to shield or weaken the magnetic field, but it is described as part of the magnetization device, not necessarily a housing portion, and its integration with the housing is not explicitly detailed.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference mentions projections but does not specify their length in relation to the workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not explicitly describe a receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles on the contact surfaces of the pole shoes.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles on the contact surfaces of the pole shoes.

claims.note: (non-English passage at abstract) This passage describes a gripping device for gripping ferromagnetic objects.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0035) The reference discloses a magnet that is displaceable between an active configuration for gripping and a passive configuration for releasing.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0036) The reference discloses contact elements that guide magnetic flux to a contact surface, but does not explicitly call them 'pole shoes' or state they are 'attached to the housing'.
The reference does not disclose a contact surface angle between the workpiece contact surface and the displacement direction, nor does it specify a range for such an angle.
The reference describes contact elements and a magnetization device, but there is no mention of a specific contact surface angle or its range.
The reference describes a gripper base body (housing) but does not explicitly state that it extends along a longitudinal axis.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0033) The quote states that the displacement axes of the contact elements are parallel to each other and to the gripping direction. However, it does not explicitly state that the displacement direction is aligned parallel to a longitudinal axis of the housing.
The reference describes contact elements that guide a magnetic field, but it does not mention an 'active structure' within each pole shoe for directing the magnetic field portion.
The reference describes contact elements that can adapt to a curved surface, but it does not mention a bevel on an active structure or a bevel angle.
The reference describes contact elements with contact surfaces, but it does not define a bevel angle between a bevel and a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not mention any specific angle ranges for a bevel angle.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0004) The quote describes contact elements with contact surfaces, which could be considered projections forming a workpiece contact surface. However, it does not explicitly state that these projections are for directing the magnetic field portion.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0030) The reference discloses a gripping device comprising a plurality of contact elements, which can be considered as projections.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0030) The reference describes multiple contact elements that are arranged adjacent to each other to form a contact surface.
The reference does not explicitly mention a recess between projections.
The reference does not specify any dimensional relationship between a recess and the length of projections.

The reference describes a gripping device with contact elements and a magnetization device, but it does not explicitly mention a separate 'positioning device' for positioning a workpiece on the contact surface.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0019) The reference describes contact elements acting as magnetic poles (south and north poles) when interacting with the magnet, which is analogous to pole shoes. However, it does not explicitly use the term 'pole shoe' for the contact elements.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0019) The quoted passage clearly states that in the active configuration, the magnet interacts with contact elements such that some provide a magnetic south pole and others a magnetic north pole.

claims.quote: Die Antriebseinrichtung kann beispielsweise pneumatisch, hydraulisch, elektrisch und/oder mechanisch betrieben sein.
claims.note: The reference explicitly states that the drive device for displacing the magnet can be operated pneumatically, hydraulically, electrically, and/or mechanically.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a drive device (Antriebseinrichtung) being operated pneumatically, hydraulically, electrically or mechanically, but does not specify that a magnet is displaceable between gripping and release positions.

claims.note: The reference does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0024) The reference discloses a sensor device, specifically presence sensors, to detect if an object is at the contact elements, which functions as a workpiece sensor.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0011) The reference mentions the gripper base body (housing) can include supply connections for external supply lines.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0011) The reference describes the gripper base body having a connecting device for attaching the gripping device to a manipulator, such as a robot flange.
The reference discusses a shielding element for the magnetic field, but not a housing portion designed to suppress its escape.

claims.quote: Es ist grundsÃ¤tzlich auch denkbar, dass die Magnetisierungseinrichtung ein Abschirmelement umfasst, welches dazu ausgebildet ist, ein von dem Magnet bereitgestelltes magnetisches Feld abzuschirmen oder abzuschwÃ¤chen.
claims.note: The reference teaches that the magnetization device can include a shielding element to shield or weaken the magnetic field provided by the magnet.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a shielding element as part of the magnetization device to shield the magnetic field, not as a separate shielding device of the magnetic gripper designed to prevent field escape from the housing.

claims.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0027) The reference describes a handling system (magnetic gripper system) comprising a manipulator and a gripping device (magnetic gripper).

(non-English passage at paragraph p0027) The reference describes a handling system (magnetic gripper system) that includes a gripping device (magnetic gripper) and is used for gripping ferromagnetic objects (workpiece).
(non-English passage at paragraph p0036) The reference teaches that in the active configuration, the magnet provides a magnetic flux through the contact elements to grip the object.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0043) The reference teaches that to release the object, the magnetization device is deactivated, and the magnet is moved from the active to the passive configuration.
The reference does not disclose any specific dimensions or relationships between the length of projections and the thickness of the workpiece.
The reference does not disclose a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: This reference discloses nearly all features and claims of the subject invention, describing a magnetic gripping device with displaceable contact elements for curved surfaces, a movable magnet for activation/deactivation, and a method of use, including specific details like parallel displacement axe
